scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: On summer nights, fireflies blink like tiny lanterns, without any heat or battery. How do they make light?

scenes.name: bio
scenes.text: Fireflies use bioluminescence, light made by a chemical reaction inside a living body.

scenes.name: recipe
scenes.text: In their tail, a chemical called luciferin reacts with oxygen, helped by an enzyme called luciferase.

scenes.name: cold
scenes.text: Almost all the energy becomes light, with very little heat. That's why it's called cold light.

scenes.name: switch
scenes.text: Fireflies control their flashes by controlling oxygen flow to the light organ.

scenes.name: talk
scenes.text: The blinking patterns are signals. Each species has its own pattern to find a mate.

scenes.name: others
scenes.text: Some mushrooms, jellyfish and deep sea fish also make their own light.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Chemicals plus oxygen make cold, living light. Follow for more on how things really work.
